RATE-PATH READ: It evaluates banks' resilience by estimating losses, net revenue, and capital levels—which provide a cushion against losses—under a hypothetical recession scenario.

The Board's stress test is one tool used to measure whether banks have adequate capital to absorb losses so that they can lend to households and businesses even in a severe recession.

This year, 32 large banks were subject to the Board's stress test.

The scenario includes a severe global recession with heightened stress in both commercial and residential real estate markets, as well as in corporate debt markets.

These stress test results will not impact large bank capital requirements.
